We demonstrate that, under an appropriate random model, the proposed algorithm recovers dictionaries in polynomial time for sparsity linear in $M$ (up to logarithmic factors). Our findings surpass existing methods by delivering a decaying error bound with respect to dimension $M$; in contrast, the best prior results for the overcomplete ($K > M$) setting achieved polynomial-time recovery in the linear regime only with constant error bounds. Numerical experiments validate these theoretical results.

Let $G = (V, E)$ be a graph containing no isolated vertices. A subset $D \subseteq V(G)$ is defined as a $k$-distance paired domination set if it serves as a $k$-distance dominating set and the subgraph induced by $D$, denoted $\langle D \rangle$, possesses a perfect matching. The $k$-distance paired domination number of $G$, represented by $\gamma_{p} ^{k}(G)$, corresponds to the smallest cardinality of such a set. This paper investigates the $k$-distance paired domination properties of the flower graph $f_{n\times m}$. Specifically, for $m, n \geq 3$, the exact values for both the paired domination number and the $2$-distance paired domination number of $f_{n\times m}$ are established.

Accurate uplink channel estimation is fundamental to the performance of cellular massive MIMO systems. However, as the number of user equipments (UEs) increases, resource sharing leads to inter-cell interference among neighboring UEs. While Minimum Mean Squared Error (MMSE) estimators can mitigate this interference, they rely on knowledge of channel covariance matrices. This paper introduces a novel estimator for low-rank channel covariance matrices by applying Generalized Eigenvalue Decomposition (GEVD) to two covariance matrices derived from uplink data. The proposed approach imposes minimal system requirements, necessitating no inter-cell communication beyond synchronization and no prior information regarding background noise. Furthermore, approximate MMSE estimators are developed based on this new covariance matrix method. Numerical simulations validate the efficacy of the proposed techniques.

This paper details the design, fabrication, and testing of a water-based cooling system developed for the Gas Electron Multiplier (GEM) based Muon Chamber (MuCh) detector within the Compressed Baryonic Matter (CBM) experiment at GSI, Germany. The system circulates cold water through channels in aluminum plates attached to GEM chambers. A feasibility study was performed on one small-scale and two full-size prototype plates. To ensure precise thermal management, a microcontroller-based unit was integrated for automatic monitoring and control of the plate surface temperature. Full-size prototypes underwent testing in a lead beam on a lead target at the CERN SPS, while a laboratory setup utilizing three prototype modules was prepared to simulate real-world conditions. The study comprehensively covers the operational principles, mechanical design, manufacturing process, and experimental results of these cooling prototypes.

Multimessenger astronomy is arguably the branch of astroparticle physics that has witnessed the most significant advancements in recent years. This manuscript reviews the current state-of-the-art, recent observations, and the prospects and challenges for the near future. We will give special emphasis to the observations carried out with neutrino telescopes.

We present a direct formulation of the Schrödinger equation for describing the diffraction of quantum particles through (nearly) planar slit-like structures. In this framework, physically relevant initial conditions and potentials are constructed using regularization techniques, allowing the solutions to be understood as generalized functions. We examine the fundamental spectral and scattering properties of these regularized solution families and offer a comparison with the more direct approximations and simplifications typically employed in physics.

In experimental sciences, researchers typically employ statistical power analyses prior to data collection to establish necessary sample sizes. However, traditional methods can be expensive when gathering data is challenging or costly. We introduce synthetic power analysis, a framework designed to estimate statistical power across different sample sizes, and we empirically evaluate its efficacy for sample size selection in cognitive neuroscience. Specifically, we generate brain imaging data using an implicit generative model conditioned on observed cognitive processes. Additionally, we propose a straightforward method to adjust statistical tests, yielding conservative results. Our empirical findings indicate that synthetic power analysis offers a cost-effective alternative to collecting pilot data, provided the proposed experiments share cognitive processes with those previously conducted.

Pionless effective field theory within a finite volume (FVEFT$_{\pi\!/}$) is examined as a tool for analyzing multi-nucleon spectra and matrix elements derived from lattice QCD (LQCD). By integrating FVEFT$_{\pi\!/}$ with the stochastic variational method, the spectra of nuclei with atomic numbers $A\in\{2,3\}$ are aligned with existing finite-volume LQCD results obtained at quark masses heavier than physical values, specifically at a pion mass of $m_\pi=806$ MeV. This alignment allows for the determination of infinite-volume binding energies via infinite-volume variational calculations. Utilizing the variational wavefunctions generated through this framework, finite-volume matrix elements for various local operators are calculated in FVEFT$_{\pi\!/}$ and matched against LQCD computations of the corresponding QCD operators within the same volume. This process determines the necessary one- and two-body EFT counterterms and facilitates the extrapolation of LQCD matrix elements to infinite volume. Illustrative examples include scalar, tensor, and axial matrix elements, along with magnetic moments and the isovector longitudinal momentum fraction.

We present HTLM, a hyper-text language model trained on an extensive web crawl. Modeling hyper-text offers several key benefits: (1) it is readily scalable in collection, (2) it delivers rich document-level and task-proximal supervision (where attributes like class and id often encode category information), and (3) it enables novel structured prompting aligned with HTML semantics (such as performing zero-shot summarization by infilling title tags for webpages containing input text). We demonstrate that pretraining with a BART-style denoising loss directly on simplified HTML yields highly effective transfer across a broad spectrum of end tasks and supervision levels. HTLM matches or surpasses the performance of similarly sized text-only language models in zero-shot prompting and classification fine-tuning benchmarks, while also establishing new state-of-the-art results for zero-shot summarization. Furthermore, we find that hyper-text prompts offer greater data efficiency for HTLM than plain text prompts do for existing models, and that HTLM is highly effective at auto-prompting itself by generating the most probable hyper-text formatting for any available training data. We will release all associated code and models to facilitate future HTLM research.

Although the Heisenberg model describing magnetic Mott insulators on planar lattices is relatively well-established for transition metal ions, the intrinsic spin-orbit coupling in 4f magnetic ions on similar structures reveals novel physics driven by significant anisotropies in both single-ion and exchange characteristics. This study identifies Yb delafossites as an optimal system for investigating these phenomena, as they host ideal Yb$^{3+}$ triangular lattice planes with pseudospin $s=1/2$ at low temperatures. Competing frustrated interactions in this system may result in a gapless spin liquid ground state lacking magnetic order, characterized by a massive linear specific heat that surpasses that of many heavy fermions. Conversely, applying a magnetic field triggers anisotropic magnetic ordering, leading to successive transitions into various long-range ordered phases. By integrating electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) and neutron scattering data with measurements of magnetic susceptibility, isothermal magnetization (up to full polarization), and specific heat, we analyze our experimental findings using a unified crystal-field and exchange model. This approach elucidates the crystal field's impact and the symmetry-adapted form of the exchange tensor, providing explicit formulas for the anisotropic g factor, temperature-dependent susceptibility, exchange-narrowed EPR linewidth, and saturation field.

This letter introduces a novel approach to approximating hypervolume contribution, formulated as an R² indicator. The core concept involves employing distinct line segments exclusively within the hypervolume contribution region for this approximation. Unlike traditional R²-based methods that approximate overall hypervolume, the proposed technique directly estimates hypervolume contribution by utilizing all direction vectors solely within the contribution region. Comprehensive experiments comparing this new method against a traditional R²-based approach, Monte Carlo sampling, and two exact methods demonstrate its superior performance. Specifically, compared to other approximation techniques, the new method excels in evaluating the hypervolume contributions of various solutions and pinpointing the one with the smallest contribution. Furthermore, relative to exact methods, it offers computational efficiency in high-dimensional spaces where those exact methods become impractical.

We investigate the geodesics of $5d$ Reissner-Nordström and nonsingular black strings, deriving a rational bound orbit taxonomy applicable to both massive and null test particles. In the timelike scenario, we demonstrate that test particles possessing high energy—sufficient to cause plunges or scattering in a standard black hole context—can nonetheless maintain bound orbits around these black strings. Our calculations of accumulated angles over corresponding radial periods reveal values exceeding those found in $4d$ analogues. Regarding the null case, we identify the presence of stable null orbits located outside their respective horizons; such orbits are absent in four dimensions except when the black hole is extremal.

Social inequalities are widespread, and this study demonstrates that as competition intensifies across various social institutions such as markets, universities, and elections, the Gini ($g$) and Kolkata ($k$) indices—two universal measures of inequality—converge. Starting from values representing equality ($g = 0$ and $k = 0.5$), these indices approach one another and eventually stabilize at an identical value of approximately $0.87$ under conditions of unrestricted competition. We suggest interpreting this convergence as a generalized extension of the century-old Pareto 80-20 law. Moreover, this alignment of indices mirrors patterns observed in self-organized critical (SOC) systems, providing quantitative evidence that supports the long-standing hypothesis of modeling interacting socio-economic systems within the SOC framework.

This study investigates the electronic and magnetic characteristics of a new Rb$_{x}$Sr$_{1-x}$C alloy. Our findings indicate that the lattice parameter changes with Rb composition, showing a deviation of approximately 0.4 {\AA} from Vegard's law. Total energy calculations suggest that Sr-rich compositions exhibit ferromagnetic ordering, whereas RbC-rich compositions display antiferromagnetic ordering, with a total magnetic moment between 2 and 3$\mu_\text{B}$ per cation. Similar to the parent compounds, RbC and SrC, the magnetism originates from the polarization of carbon $p$-orbitals. Spin-polarized calculations confirm half-metallicity in the alloy for $x<0.875$. Furthermore, unlike the pure parent compounds, the semiconducting spin component exhibits a direct band gap.

We utilize N-body simulations to assess the stability of triaxial models within Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND). These models feature central densities proportional to $r^{-1}$ and outer densities scaling as $r^{-4}$. Spanning a total mass range of $10^8\Msun$ to $10^{10}\Msun$, the models correspond to dwarf and medium-mass elliptical galaxies, covering regimes from deep MOND to quasi-Newtonian gravity. Constructed via the Schwarzschild method, the systems were evolved over 200 Keplerian dynamical times at a characteristic scale of 1.0 kpc. Our results indicate that the systems undergo virial overheating and settle into a quasi-equilibrium state, with relaxation occurring in approximately 5 Keplerian dynamical times. Post-relaxation, the inertial (kinetic) energy changes by less than 10% (20%) for all systems. However, the relaxation process flattens the central density profile, and the overall axis ratios shift by about 10% over the 200-time evolution. Ultimately, we confirm that the systems remain stable once equilibrium is achieved.

This paper introduces DuaIM-3DNet, a deep learning-based signal detector designed for dual-mode index modulation-based three-dimensional orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (DM-IM-3D-OFDM). In this scheme, DM-IM-3D-OFDM transmits data bits through both dual-mode 3D constellation symbols and the indices of active subcarriers. Consequently, when employing the conventional maximum likelihood (ML) detector, this approach yields superior error performance compared to existing index modulation schemes; however, the ML detector incurs high computational complexity, particularly as system parameters grow. To resolve this challenge, we propose utilizing a deep neural network (DNN) at the receiver to reliably and jointly detect both symbol and index bits for DM-IM-3D-OFDM under Rayleigh fading channels in a data-driven framework. Simulation results indicate that the proposed DNN detector achieves near-optimal performance with significantly reduced runtime complexity relative to the ML detector.

Formulated by Bernhard Riemann in 1859 as one of the Millennium Prize Problems, the Riemann Hypothesis was originally proposed to elucidate the distribution of prime numbers. This expository article explores the Deep Riemann Hypothesis for the general linear group $\mathrm{GL}_{n}$, a conjecture introduced by the third author that suggests the convergence of partial Euler products of $L$-functions along the critical line. Applications of this hypothesis include refining the error term in the Prime Number Theorem—beyond what the standard Riemann Hypothesis offers—and confirming a phenomenon analogous to Chebyshev's bias regarding Satake parameters. The primary objective of defining the Deep Riemann Hypothesis is to overcome the complexities and limitations associated with the traditional Riemann Hypothesis.

This report details a search for a new heavy scalar or pseudo-scalar Higgs boson ($H/A$) produced in association with top quark pairs, where the Higgs decays into a top-antitop pair ($H/A \rightarrow t\bar{t}$). The analysis focuses on final states containing either two same-sign leptons or at least three leptons. Data from 139 fb$^{-1}$ of proton-proton collisions at a center-of-mass energy of 13 TeV, recorded by the ATLAS detector at the LHC, were analyzed. To distinguish signal from background, two multivariate classifiers were employed. No significant deviation from Standard Model predictions was observed. Within the framework of a type-II two-Higgs-doublet model, 95% confidence level upper limits on the $t\bar{t}H/A$ production cross-section times the branching ratio for $H/A \rightarrow t\bar{t}$ were established, ranging from 6 (5) fb to 14 (10) fb for masses between 400 GeV and 1000 GeV, respectively. If only a single particle ($H$ or $A$) contributes to the $t\bar{t}t\bar{t}$ final state, $\tan\beta$ values below 1.2 or 0.5 are excluded for masses of 400 GeV and 1000 GeV, respectively; these exclusions tighten to $\tan\beta$ below 1.6 or 0.6 when both particles are considered.

This paper introduces a systematic new approach to black box group methods within computational group theory. Beginning with the construction of Frobenius maps on black box groups of untwisted Lie type in odd characteristic, we apply these maps to black box groups $X$ representing $(P)SL(2,q)$ in small odd characteristics. We present an algorithm that constructs a black box field $K$ isomorphic to $\mathbb{F}_q$, along with an isomorphism mapping $(P)SL(2,K)$ to $X$. This algorithm operates in time quadratic in the field's characteristic and polynomial in $\log q$. Additionally, given the nature of our work, we address several methodological concerns inherent to black box group theory.

This research addresses remote state estimation when a passive eavesdropper is present within a network lacking packet acknowledgment mechanisms. In this setup, a legitimate remote user attempts to estimate the state of a linear plant using data transmitted from a sensor over an insecure and unreliable channel, which is susceptible to interception. To ensure state confidentiality, we introduce an encoding strategy that activates upon eavesdropper detection. This method involves the random transmission of noise governed by a pre-established pseudo-random indicator shared between the legitimate user and the sensor. By injecting noise, the scheme degrades the eavesdropper's estimation capabilities while simultaneously minimizing performance loss for the legitimate user. We further analyze the trade-off between maintaining state secrecy and the extent of performance degradation experienced by the legitimate user.

The QUBIC (Q & U bolometric interferometer for cosmology) prototype underwent laboratory testing at the Astroparticle Physics and Cosmology laboratory in Paris. Its detection chain consists of 256 NbSi transition edge sensors (TES) operating at 320 mK. The readout utilizes a 128:1 time domain multiplexing architecture featuring 128 SQUIDs cooled to 1 K, which are managed and amplified by an SiGe application-specific integrated circuit at 40 K. This report details the performance of the readout chain and the characterization of the TES. Both functional tests and characterizations were conducted in the lab and on the QUBIC instrument. The low noise amplifier achieved a white noise floor of 0.3 nV.Hz^-0.5. Characterization of the QUBIC detectors and readout electronics involved measuring I-V curves, time constants, and noise equivalent power. Approximately 80% of the QUBIC TES bolometer array operates within required parameters. The system demonstrated thermal decoupling compatible with a phonon noise level of roughly 5.10^-17 W.Hz^-0.5 at a critical temperature of 410 mK. Although currently constrained by microphonics from pulse tubes and noise aliasing from the readout, the instrument's noise equivalent power stands at approximately 2.10^-16 W.Hz^-0.5, which is sufficient to demonstrate bolometric interferometry.

We introduce an explicit formula for Lorentz boosts and rotations that commute with BMS supertranslations in asymptotically flat spacetimes. Central to this construction are infrared regularizations and a unitary transformation ensuring observables commute with soft degrees of freedom. We explicitly confirm that our charges adhere to the Lorentz algebra and validate their consistency by evaluating them on supertranslated Minkowski space and the boosted Kerr black hole.

The three-dimensional Anderson model, a prominent framework for disordered electron systems exhibiting the delocalization-localization transition, is analyzed in this work. Building on our prior studies of 2D and 3D quantum phase transitions [J. Phys. Soc. Jpn. {\bf 85}, 123706 (2016), {\bf 86}, 044708 (2017)], we employed an image recognition algorithm utilizing a multilayered convolutional neural network. Unlike our earlier applications of 2D image recognition, this study implements 3D image recognition to examine complete 3D wave functions. We demonstrate that training a 3D convolutional neural network at the band center enables the construction of a comprehensive phase diagram across the disorder-energy plane. Furthermore, we show that the full phase diagrams for both 3D quantum bond and site percolation models can be generated through training on the 3D Anderson model at the band center.

Non-fullerene acceptor (NFA) materials have established new paradigms for organic solar cell (OSC) design, enabling efficient carrier generation with minimal driving forces to maximize open-circuit voltage. This study employs a coarse-grained mixed quantum-classical approach, integrating Ehrenfest and Redfield theories, to elucidate the charge generation process at interfaces with small energy offsets. We examined how energetic driving forces and vibronic effects influence charge generation and photovoltaic energy conversion. By analyzing Holstein and Peierls vibrational couplings, we determined that vibrational coupling generally enhances charge generation; however, the mechanisms differ: Holstein relaxation reduces charge generation, whereas the Peierls mechanism consistently facilitates it. Furthermore, our analysis of electron-hole binding energy over time reveals two distinct charge separation regimes: a temperature-independent excitonic spread occurring within sub-100 femtoseconds, and the complete dissociation of the charge-transfer state taking place over tens to hundreds of picoseconds, contingent on temperature. Finally, the system's quantum dynamics display the three regimes of Marcus electron transfer kinetics as the interface energy offset varies.

Microservice Architectures (MSA), recognized for managing complex software systems, are becoming the leading paradigm in automotive software development. Effective MSA design necessitates proper system decomposition and component communication, requiring a blend of software expertise and domain knowledge. To address these needs, we created the helyOS framework, a specialized MSA solution tailored for autonomous driving applications within specific areas. This framework breaks down complex applications into predefined microservice domains and establishes a communication backbone for event messaging and data exchange. The paper illustrates how this customized MSA framework expedites development by enabling rapid integration of motion planning algorithms, device controllers, vehicle simulators, and web-browser interfaces.

Conventional analytic continuation techniques relying on maximum entropy or sparsity often encounter challenges due to ill-posed kernel matrices or require extensive computation for parameter tuning. In this work, we introduce a neural network approach grounded in convex optimization that substitutes the problematic inverse problem with a series of well-conditioned surrogate tasks. Post-training, the derived optimizers deliver high-quality solutions with minimal computational overhead and demonstrate superior parameter efficiency compared to heuristic fully-connected networks. Furthermore, the generated output can serve as a neural prior to enhance maximum entropy performance. These methods are readily adaptable to other high-dimensional inverse problems through large-scale pretraining.

Progress in manufacturing and characterizing complex molecular architectures has necessitated novel design strategies at the molecular scale. While emerging methods increasingly depend on Artificial Intelligence (AI) trained on extensive data libraries, this shift, despite yielding successful results, still faces hurdles regarding interpretability and generalizability. This work investigates an alternative framework that integrates AI with physics-based principles for molecular and materials engineering. In this approach, machine learning (ML) models trained on data from a single system are used to construct collective variables, similar to those employed in enhanced sampling simulations. These ML-derived variables allow for the identification of pivotal molecular interactions, whose modulation facilitates the systematic reshaping of the system's free energy landscape. To demonstrate the method's effectiveness, we applied it to engineer allosteric regulation and uniaxial strain fluctuations within a complex disordered elastic network. The successful implementation in these scenarios offers insights into functionality control in highly connected systems and highlights the potential for designing intricate molecular structures.

Projected entangled pair states (PEPS) extended to the thermodynamic limit (iPEPS) already yield highly accurate ground-state results for two-dimensional systems via variational optimization or imaginary-time evolution. In this work, we demonstrate (i) the viability of employing real-time evolution within the iPEPS framework to model the dynamics of infinite systems following a global quench, and (ii) the utility of disorder-averaging techniques for handling translationally invariant systems subjected to disorder. As a demonstration of this methodology, we analyze the short-time dynamics of the square lattice Heisenberg model under the influence of a bi-valued disorder field.

The narrative progression in novels is evident through its content and vocabulary. Since the flow of sentiments—a key component of writing style—can be measured by analyzing word sequences, this study examines literary works as signals within word embedding spaces to compare the stylistic approaches of popular classic novels using dynamic time warping.

Using the LHCb detector, researchers measured the production fraction of $B_c^-$ mesons relative to the sum of $B^-$ and $\bar{B}^0$ mesons in $pp$ collisions at both 7 and 13 TeV center-of-mass energies provided by the Large Hadron Collider. This rate, which is roughly 3.7 per mille, remains constant across energy levels but exhibits a dependence on transverse momentum. Additionally, the asymmetry in $B_c^- - B_c^+$ production was found to be consistent with zero, falling within the statistical and systematic uncertainties of a few percent.

**Purpose:** Locating and segmenting individual bones serves as a critical preprocessing stage for numerous planning and navigation systems. However, performing this task manually is both time-intensive and repetitive, a challenge that affects not only clinical workflows but also the gathering of training data. Consequently, we introduce an end-to-end learning algorithm capable of segmenting 125 distinct bones within upper-body CT scans, alongside an ensemble-based uncertainty metric designed to identify specific scans for expanding the training dataset.

**Methods:** We generate fully automated segmentations using a neural network architecture derived from the 3D-Unet, employing fully supervised training. Performance is enhanced through the use of ensembles and inference-time augmentation. Furthermore, we analyze the correlation between ensemble uncertainty and the potential utility of unlabelled scans for dataset expansion.

**Results:** The methodology is evaluated on an internal dataset comprising 16 upper-body CT scans, each with a resolution of 2 mm per dimension. Considering all 125 bones in our label set, our top-performing ensemble achieves a median Dice Similarity Coefficient (DSC) of 0.83. Our findings indicate no correlation between a scan's ensemble uncertainty and its future impact on accuracy when added to an enlarged training set. Conversely, we demonstrate that ensemble uncertainty correlates with the volume of voxels requiring manual correction following initial automated segmentation, thereby reducing the time needed to finalize new ground truth labels.

**Conclusion:** Collectively, scans exhibiting low ensemble uncertainty require less annotator effort while offering comparable improvements in future DSC metrics. Therefore, they represent ideal candidates for expanding a training set dedicated to segmenting distinct bones in upper-body CT scans.

Given the lack of an effective treatment or vaccine and an incomplete understanding of the epidemiological cycle, the Government enacted a nationwide lockdown in India to curb the spread of COVID-19. To evaluate the impact of social distancing, we developed a novel mathematical model integrating lockdown effects. By validating this model against notified case data from five states and India as a whole, we estimated key epidemiological parameters, including the basic reproduction number ($R_{0}$). Merging our mechanistic model with various statistical forecasting methods, we projected notified cases for six locations between May 17 and May 31, 2020. A global sensitivity analysis was conducted to assess how two measurable epidemiological parameters influence the lockdown's effectiveness and $R_{0}$. Our findings indicate that lockdowns are most effective in areas with a higher proportion of symptomatic infections. Additionally, large-scale mass testing is necessary to mitigate community transmission. Ensemble model forecasts predicted a significant surge in notified cases in most locations in the near future. Furthermore, the trend of the effective reproduction number ($R_{t}$) during the projection period suggests that if lockdown measures were completely lifted after May 17, 2020, a sharp spike in cases could occur in those regions. Finally, synthesizing these results, we formulated an effective lockdown policy to minimize future COVID-19 transmission in India.

We demonstrate that quantum DT invariants for quivers equipped with gentle potentials can be formulated using specific refined enumerations of tropical disks. This result relies on a quantum adaptation of Bridgeland's framework for describing cluster scattering diagrams via stability conditions, alongside a novel approach to characterizing scattering diagrams through tropical disk counts. The weights assigned to these tropical disks are defined by motivic integrals over particular quiver flag varieties. Furthermore, we provide an explicit counterexample showing that Hall algebra broken lines fail to yield consistent Hall algebra theta functions, thereby contradicting the extension of a lemma by Carl-Pumperla-Siebert from the classical context.

Identifying burn scars caused by wildfires in remote rainforests is crucial for disaster management and ecological research. However, the complex, fragmented nature of agricultural landscapes and varied crop types often hinder accurate mapping of these scars. While recent advancements in remote sensing and the availability of multimodal data provide a potential solution, segmenting burn marks remains challenging due to their visual similarity to other land patterns, their highly fragmented structure, and the presence of noise in partially labeled datasets. This study introduces AmazonNET, a convolutional neural network designed to extract burn patterns from multimodal remote sensing imagery. The architecture adapts the well-established UNet framework—an encoder-decoder model with skip connections typically used in biomedical segmentation. By leveraging stacked RGB-NIR channels, the proposed framework segments burn scars from pastures using a newly created, weakly labeled noisy dataset from the Amazon region. The model demonstrates superior performance by accurately identifying partially labeled burn scars and filtering out mislabeled samples, marking it as one of the pioneering applications of deep learning-based segmentation for multimodal burn scar detection.

The joint effort of the MOSDEF and KBSS-MOSFIRE surveys marks the largest cumulative allocation of Keck/MOSFIRE observing time, covering approximately 3,000 galaxies within the redshift range of 1.4 to 3.8, with roughly half located at z~2. MOSDEF selects targets based on photometric and spectroscopic redshifts alongside a rest-optical magnitude limit, whereas KBSS-MOSFIRE primarily relies on rest-UV colors and magnitude limits. By analyzing both datasets uniformly using consistent spectral-energy-distribution (SED) models, we observe that the MOSDEF z~2 targeted sample exhibits a higher median stellar mass (M_*) and redder rest U-V colors compared to the KBSS-MOSFIRE z~2 sample. Furthermore, MOSDEF targets show lower median star formation rates (SFR(SED)) and specific star formation rates (sSFR(SED)). Specifically, MOSDEF focused on a larger population of red galaxies (U-V and V-J >= 1.25), while KBSS-MOSFIRE captured more young galaxies undergoing intense star formation. Despite these distinctions in their z~2 targeted samples, the subsets containing multiple detected emission lines analyzed in prior publications are remarkably similar. With the exception of stellar population age, all median host-galaxy properties—including M_*, SFR(SED), sSFR(SED), A_V, and UVJ colors—agree within uncertainties. Additionally, applying uniform emission-line fitting and stellar Balmer absorption corrections eliminates significant offsets between the two samples in the [OIII]$\lambda$5008/H$\beta$ vs. [NII]$\lambda$6585/H$\alpha$ diagnostic diagram, resolving previously reported discrepancies. Consequently, we can now merge the MOSDEF and KBSS-MOSFIRE surveys to create the largest z~2 sample featuring moderate-resolution rest-optical spectra, enabling the construction of fundamental scaling relations for star-forming galaxies during this critical epoch.

Deep learning-driven joint source-channel coding (JSCC) has demonstrated superior efficacy in transmitting images and features. Nevertheless, the continuous nature of JSCC encoder outputs creates a complex and dense modulation constellation, rendering the design of radio frequency chains capable of handling these full-resolution points both difficult and costly. This paper introduces two techniques for mapping full-resolution constellations to finite ones, facilitating practical system deployment. One method yields a regular constellation, while the other produces an irregular one. These approaches were integrated into existing deep JSCC architectures and tested on AWGN channels across various signal-to-noise ratios (SNRs). Experimental findings indicate that the proposed methods surpass traditional uniform quadrature amplitude modulation (QAM) mapping with minimal additional parameters.

Origami-based mechanical metamaterials have garnered considerable scientific attention recently because of their adaptable and reconfigurable structures. Nevertheless, accounting for every potential geometric configuration becomes difficult when each origami unit can assume multiple phases. In this study, we examine the reconfigurability of a tessellation made from bellows-like origami unit cells, specifically the Tachi-Miura Polyhedron (TMP). A distinctive characteristic of the TMP is its ability for a single cell to transition through four distinct phases while maintaining rigid foldability, allowing the resulting tessellation to form various shapes from an initial assembly. To validate the geometric feasibility of the vast number of possible phase combinations, we develop a graph-theoretical framework to model unit cell connectivity and analyze tessellation reconfigurability. This methodology establishes a foundation for creating systematic computational tools to design origami-based mechanical metamaterials with customized properties.

We examine an extension of modal $\mu$-calculus incorporating sets with atoms and investigate its fundamental characteristics. While model checking remains decidable on orbit-finite structures and corresponds to parity games, satisfiability becomes undecidable. Furthermore, we demonstrate the expressive constraints of atom-enriched $\mu$-calculi, detailing how their power varies based on the atomic structure employed and the selection of either basic or vectorial syntax.

Hansen's disease, also known as leprosy, is a neglected tropical infectious disease caused by the bacterium *Mycobacterium leprae*. Globally, approximately 202,189 new cases are identified annually; in 2017 alone, over half a million individuals suffered from leprosy-induced disability, with nearly 50,000 new cases emerging each year. Nerve damage resulting from lepra reactions is the primary driver of disability in leprosy patients. Consequently, early detection of these reactions via biomarker analysis plays a critical role in preventing future impairments. To date, literature regarding within-host cellular-level modeling of crucial biomarkers and optimal drug regimens for leprosy and its reactions remains scarce. Driven by this gap, this study introduces and analyzes a three-dimensional mathematical model that simulates the dynamics of susceptible Schwann cells, infected Schwann cells, and bacterial load, reflecting the disease's pathogenesis. Parameters were estimated from clinical literature to enhance the model's practicality. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using the Partial Rank Correlation Coefficient (PRCC) to identify the most influential single parameter and pairs of parameters, while the Sobol index was applied to evaluate the remaining parameters. Furthermore, an optimal control problem was formulated, treating Multi-Drug Therapy (MDT) components as control variables, and later expanded to include both MDT and steroid interventions. These findings from this novel and comprehensive study aim to assist clinicians and public health researchers in the efforts to eliminate and eradicate leprosy.

We introduce two novel concepts, the dynamically transversely trapping surface (DTTS) and the marginally DTTS, to serve as markers for regions of strong gravity. A DTTS is characterized as a closed, two-dimensional surface on a spacelike hypersurface where photons emitted transversely from any point undergo accelerated contraction over time; in spherically symmetric scenarios, a marginally DTTS corresponds to the photon sphere. These structures share significant similarities with (marginally) trapped surfaces. Following the development of solution methods for marginally DTTSs in both time-symmetric and momentarily stationary axisymmetric initial data, we numerically constructed examples for binary black hole systems within the Brill-Lindquist and Majumdar-Papapetrou spacetimes. We further demonstrated that the area of a DTTS satisfies a Penrose-like inequality, $A_0\le 4\pi (3GM)^2$, subject to specific conditions. The text also explores the distinctions and relationships between the DTTS and two previously proposed concepts: the loosely trapped surface [arXiv:1701.00564] and the static/stationary transversely trapping surface [arXiv:1704.04637]. Ultimately, the (marginally) DTTS offers a theoretical framework to deepen our comprehension of strong gravity fields. Moreover, because DTTSs reside outside the event horizon, they may hold relevance for future observations of strong gravity regions during dynamical evolutions.
We calculate the Ext-algebra for a Brauer tree algebra corresponding to a line lacking an exceptional vertex.

A primary objective in non-equilibrium statistical mechanics is to comprehend how hydrodynamic behavior arises from the unitary evolution of the many-particle Schrödinger equation. This study presents a digital simulation of the discrete-time quantum dynamics of a spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ XXZ chain on a noisy, near-term quantum processor, specifically extracting the high-temperature transport exponent at the isotropic point. We model the temporal decay of relevant spin correlation functions at high temperatures using a pseudo-random state produced by a random circuit optimized for the IBMQ-Montreal 27-qubit device. The simulation yields a spin excitation set against a highly inhomogeneous background. By analyzing the subsequent discrete-time dynamics on the hardware, we derive an anomalous super-diffusive exponent that aligns with the conjectured Kardar-Parisi-Zhang (KPZ) scaling at the isotropic point. Additionally, we demonstrate the recovery of spin diffusion by applying a potential that breaks integrability.

This research investigates phonon angular momentum within magnetic crystals, revealing that spin-phonon interactions generate a nonzero angular momentum that behaves as an odd function of magnetization. At absolute zero, phonons possess both zero-point energy and zero-point angular momentum. As temperature rises, the total phonon angular momentum decreases, vanishing in the classical limit. This phenomenon significantly influences the Einstein-de Haas effect; specifically, determining the change in electron angular momentum requires subtracting the phonon angular momentum change from the opposing change in lattice angular momentum. Additionally, these findings offer a novel approach to studying spin-phonon interactions, with potential experimental methods for detecting phonon angular momentum also explored.

Reusing established datasets holds significant value for researchers and developers, with search engines playing a crucial role in locating relevant resources. These engines often display snippets to clarify how each dataset aligns with a user's specific needs. However, the challenge of generating such snippets for dataset searches has garnered little academic attention. To lay the groundwork for future studies, we propose a framework for quantitatively assessing snippet quality. The introduced metrics measure how well a snippet aligns with query intent and comprehensively covers the dataset's primary content. To set a baseline, we adapted four state-of-the-art techniques from related domains, conducting an empirical evaluation using real-world data and queries, alongside a user study to validate our results. Our findings confirm the effectiveness of this evaluation framework and offer insights for subsequent research directions.

Ultrafast Electron Diffractometers (UEDs) and Free-Electron Lasers (FELs) depend on high-brightness electron beams generated by radio-frequency (RF) photocathode guns. To enable the next generation of high-repetition-rate UEDs and FELs, which demand high average brightness, we present a continuous wave RF photocathode gun operating at 325 MHz with an APEX-like geometry. This device produces electron beams with exceptional peak and average 5D brightness while maintaining moderate RF power usage. Operated in the blowout regime with a 0.4 MeV energy gain and a peak cathode field of 35 MV/m, the gun was analyzed through extensive numerical simulations across three operational regimes: (i) 160 fC beams with 5-nm emittance for UEDs, (ii) 1.6 pC beams with 20-nm emittance for table-top FELs and dielectric accelerators, and (iii) 16 pC beams with 50-nm emittance for inverse Compton sources and other photon accelerators. We also developed a straightforward analytical model describing virtual cathode formation—the suppression of photoemission current caused by space-charge forces—which incorporates laser pulse duration. Our simulations reveal a distinct maximum in 5D beam brightness when the laser spot radius is approximately 150% of the critical radius where the virtual cathode begins to form. This result contradicts the prevailing literature view that, in the blowout regime, the laser spot radius must be significantly larger than the critical radius associated with virtual cathode onset.

Straight-bladed cross-flow turbines transform kinetic energy from wind or water flows into mechanical power. However, unlike axial-flow turbines, the impact of geometric variables on their efficiency remains poorly understood due to a lack of universal analytical equations and affordable, precise numerical simulations for their fluid dynamics. This study experimentally examines how the aspect ratio—the ratio of blade span to rotor diameter—affects the performance of such a turbine within a water channel. To ensure the aspect ratio was the sole variable, all other non-dimensional parameters, including relative confinement, Froude number, and Reynolds number, were kept constant. Results indicate that the coefficient of performance remains consistent across the tested aspect ratio range (0.95 to 1.63), attributed to negligible blade-support interactions in this specific design. Furthermore, when a subset of experiments was conducted without regulating the Froude number, the coefficient of performance increased; this rise resulted from Froude number fluctuations that could be erroneously attributed to changes in aspect ratio. These findings underscore the necessity of rigorous experimental design when analyzing how geometric parameters influence cross-flow turbine performance.

Enhanced octupole collectivity is anticipated in neutron-deficient Ge, Se, and Kr isotopes near $N \approx 40$, a phenomenon confirmed in $^{70,72}$Ge. However, theoretical models struggle to predict octupole collectivity in this mass region due to the notorious complexities of shape coexistence and configuration mixing, which involve rapid variations in nuclear shape as nucleon number and spin change. To investigate the microscopic configurations driving the prolate-oblate-triaxial shape transition at $A \approx 72$ and their impact on octupole collectivity, researchers examined the rare isotopes $^{72}$Se and $^{74,76}$Kr using inelastic proton scattering in inverse kinematics. The study revealed significantly enhanced octupole strength of approximately 32 Weisskopf units (W.u.) for $^{72}$Se, compared to only about 15 W.u. for $^{74,76}$Kr. When combined with existing data, these findings challenge the notion of a simple origin for enhanced octupole strengths around $N = 40$. This work identifies two distinct regions of octupole strength, separated by a sudden increase near the $A=72$ shape transitional point.

This chapter is part of the forthcoming monograph "Out of Nowhere: The Emergence of Spacetime in Quantum Theories of Gravity," co-authored by Nick Huggett and Christian Wüthrich and published by Oxford University Press. Additional details are available at https://beyondspacetime.net/. The chapter outlines the problem of spacetime emergence within quantum gravity, presents the primary philosophical challenge associated with it, and proposes our favored resolution.

This piece presents a brief and engaging collection of unresolved issues in Plane Geometry. Although the statements appear simple and accessible to elementary readers, their solutions have remained elusive for the best part of four decades.

A convex geometric hypergraph (cgh) is defined by a collection of subsets derived from a strictly convex set of points in the plane. While extremal problems for cghs have been widely researched, this paper investigates their associated saturation problems. We provide an asymptotic determination of the saturation number for two geometrically disjoint $r$-tuples. Additionally, regarding the eight nonisomorphic $3$-uniform cghs on two edges, we establish the saturation number for seven of them up to a constant factor and the eighth up to a logarithmic factor.

Scalar leptoquarks represent leading candidates for resolving intriguing indications of lepton flavour universality violation. Specifically, the $SU(2)_L$ scalar leptoquark doublet $S_2$ can address discrepancies between Standard Model predictions and experimental measurements in $(g-2)_\mu$, $b\to s\ell^+ \ell^-$, $b\to c\tau\nu$ transitions, and non-resonant di-electron production. However, a minimal framework featuring only one leptoquark generation fails to simultaneously explain these phenomena, as it would induce excessively large charged lepton flavour violation. Consequently, we introduce a model comprising three generations of $S_2$, where each generation couples strictly to a specific lepton flavour, thereby extending the Standard Model with distinct electroquark, muoquark, and tauquark particles. We demonstrate that, even after accounting for additional constraints from electroweak precision observables and $\Delta F=2$ processes, this framework successfully offers a unified explanation for all observed violations of lepton flavour universality. Furthermore, the inclusion of the tauquark enables the generation of a dimension-six ${\cal O}_9^U$ operator through off-shell photon penguin diagrams; combined with the muoquark contribution, this significantly enhances the global fit to $b \to s \ell^+ \ell^-$ data.

Low-quality music recordings, often captured by consumer devices like smartphones, frequently suffer from distortions such as background noise, reverberation, and microphone-induced equalization. This study introduces a deep learning framework to improve such audio by integrating an image-to-image translation model that processes audio in mel-spectrogram form with a music vocoder that converts these synthetic spectrograms into perceptually accurate waveforms. Our results demonstrate that this method surpasses existing baselines, including those relying on classical mel-spectrogram inversion techniques and end-to-end models that directly map noisy waveforms to clean ones. Furthermore, listening tests evaluating this approach reveal insights into the reliability of standard audio enhancement metrics specifically within the music domain.

New developments in quantum hardware present novel methods for tackling optimization challenges that are computationally intensive for classical systems. We introduce a hybrid algorithm designed for portfolio optimization, which transforms Markowitz's Mean-Variance Model into a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem while integrating expected shortfall as a risk metric to enhance performance during market extremes. Utilizing real-world financial data, we evaluated the algorithm on D-Wave's 2000Q and Advantage quantum annealers, finding that both devices successfully generated portfolios exceeding 80% of the classical optimal solutions. Furthermore, our results indicate that assets with higher correlations yield better performance, a finding that could inform the development of practical quantum applications in the near future.

Although Shor's algorithm offers a theoretical path to simplifying prime factorization on quantum computers, its potential remains unrealized due to qubit noise and insufficient error correction. This work investigates a viable alternative approach based on variational imaginary time evolution. By constructing a Hamiltonian whose ground state represents the factorization solution, we iteratively evolve an initial state toward the prime factors using variational methods. Our analysis demonstrates that the circuit evaluations per iteration scale as O(n^{5}d), with n denoting the bit-length of the target number and d representing the circuit depth. We successfully factorized numbers encoded in 7-, 8-, and 9-qubit Hamiltonians using a single layer of entangling gates, and validated the method's efficacy through implementation on the IBMQ Lima quantum processor.

This study examines an oscillator algebra characterized by four parameters: $p$, $q$, $\alpha$, and $\nu$. It provides explicit analytic solutions for the energy spectrum derived from the time-independent Schrödinger equation of the induced deformed harmonic oscillator. The work constructs and evaluates deformed states based on coherent state criteria. Additionally, it calculates and analyzes various commutators involving creation and annihilation operators, along with their combinatorial properties. Finally, it determines the correlation functions of matrix elements for both normal and antinormal forms, which are essential for quantum optics analysis.

This paper surveys several data visualization methods designed to analyze Computer Vision (CV) datasets. By conducting dataset-level analyses, these techniques reveal inherent properties and latent patterns within the data. We illustrate how such analyses can forecast the influence of dataset characteristics on CV model performance and guide the mitigation of associated weaknesses. Furthermore, we investigate future directions for visualization approaches tailored to various modalities of CV data and specific analytical requirements.

In 1921, Mellin published a *Comptes Rendu* article that calculated the principal root of the polynomial $Z^n + x_1Z^{n_1} + \cdots + x_pZ^{n_p} - 1$ via hypergeometric functions dependent on its coefficients $x_1, \dots, x_p$, employing an integral transform now known as the Mellin transform. Spanning just over three pages in a concise French style characteristic of the language, the paper remains difficult to explain elementarily, as no such explanation exists in current textbooks or online. To render Mellin's significant finding accessible to those without specialized expertise in hypergeometric functions or complex analysis, we have composed this expository article.

Term pattern matching involves identifying all occurrences of patterns within a subject term based on a provided set of patterns, making the development of efficient algorithms for this task a key research focus [19]. We introduce a novel set automaton approach to the term pattern matching problem, grounded in match set derivatives, which ensures each function symbol in the subject pattern is visited precisely once. This algorithm supports diverse traversal strategies over the subject term and is especially well-suited for parallel searching.

We introduce a structural attack targeting the DME cryptosystem configured with parameters (3,2,q). This method successfully recovers 10 out of the 12 coefficients comprising the first linear map. Furthermore, we demonstrate that possessing knowledge of all 12 coefficients allows for the efficient derivation of the remaining private key components by solving systems of quadratic equations involving only two variables.

This research aims to enhance our understanding of how the Point of Release (PoR) influences the perception of animated throwing actions. We present findings from a perceptual study in which participants observed virtual humans throwing a ball with the PoR manipulated to occur either early or late. Our results indicate that timing errors in overarm throws are more readily detected when the PoR is late, whereas the opposite holds true for underarm throws. Additionally, both the viewing angle and the distance the ball travels impact perceived realism. These insights can be utilized to increase the plausibility of throwing animations in interactive environments, such as video games and virtual reality applications.

Music recommender systems are now integral to major streaming services like Spotify, Pandora, and Last.fm, aiding users in discovering music aligned with their tastes. These systems analyze historical listening data to predict future musical preferences. Current methodologies primarily rely on collaborative filtering (CF) by identifying similarities in user behavior, with some hybrid models integrating content-based features alongside CF. Although these systems effectively suggest music for mainstream artists, recent studies indicate a bias against listeners of niche or non-mainstream acts. This disparity stems largely from the scarcity of consumption data for less popular music, as user patterns heavily favor mainstream hits. Consequently, this work aims to introduce a novel method for modeling artist preferences across diverse user listening habits and consumption patterns.

Soft elastic substrates display wetting characteristics absent in rigid systems. Modeling these complex elastocapillary interactions has historically been restricted to isolated contact lines or single drops. We introduce a reduced long-wave model that effectively captures the essential qualitative aspects of both static and dynamic soft wetting, extending applicability to droplet ensembles. Formulated as gradient dynamics on a free energy landscape incorporating capillarity, wettability, and compressional elasticity, the model successfully recovers the double transition in equilibrium contact angles observed as substrates soften from rigid to liquid-like states. Furthermore, it accurately reproduces established dependencies of dynamic contact angles on contact line velocity for both partially and completely wetting liquids. Finally, moving beyond single droplets, we analyze coarsening in two-drop systems and large ensembles, demonstrating that the dominant coarsening mode shifts nontrivially with substrate softness.

This paper introduces a three-dimensional discrete framework for analyzing the deformation of a viral capsid, modeled as a regular icosahedron resting on a flat rigid surface at a single vertex. Initially, we formulate the model as a system of variational inequalities defined over a non-empty, closed, and convex subset of an appropriate function space. Subsequently, we demonstrate the existence and uniqueness of the solution for this model. Finally, numerical simulations are conducted to validate the approach, revealing that the results align with physical principles.

This study measured the angular distributions and energy spectra of $\alpha$ particles and deuterons resulting from breakup, transfer, and incomplete fusion processes to distinguish their individual contributions and assess the significance of breakup-fusion relative to transfer mechanisms. Inclusive $\alpha$ production cross-sections were measured for the $^6$Li + $^{51}$V system near Coulomb barrier energies, supported by theoretical calculations using the finite range coupled reaction method via the \textsc{FRESCO} code. These calculations estimated contributions from non-capture breakup ($\alpha$ + \textit{d}), 1\textit{n}, 1\textit{p}, and 1\textit{d} transfer channels, compound nuclear decay, and incomplete fusion (ICF) to determine cumulative production cross-sections. The combined contributions from breakup, transfer, and incomplete fusion channels successfully reproduced the integral direct $\alpha$ production cross-sections and their angular distributions. These direct $\alpha$ cross-sections align with data from other targets and are notably higher than deuteron production cross-sections. Kinematic analysis of the energy spectra indicates that $\alpha$ particle spectra are primarily dominated by breakup-fusion, whereas deuteron spectra involve contributions from both breakup and transfer reactions. A systematic study of direct $\alpha$ production across various targets reveals an average universal behavior, though distinct differences exist among specific targets. Furthermore, the ratio of $\alpha$ to deuteron yields across a wide mass range of targets demonstrates saturation above the barrier and an increasing relative production of $\alpha$ particles around the Coulomb barrier.

This paper investigates investment markets structured as networks, where each agent (vertex) can invest in connected enterprises while simultaneously raising capital from its linked counterparts. If an agent fails to secure adequate funding, its firm defaults, preventing further investment. The primary goal is to analyze how collateral contracts mitigate strategic risks that could escalate into systemic risk via default cascades. Using a mechanism-design framework, we determine the optimal collateral scheme that capital providers offer to investors. These contracts are designed to maintain efficient investment levels as the sole Nash equilibrium while minimizing total collateral requirements.

Our findings contrast network environments with non-network settings, where investors and capital raisers are distinct groups. We demonstrate that in acyclic investment networks, the network structure does not require additional collateral beyond optimal bilateral contracts between capital raisers and their investors to manage systemic risk. However, this does not hold for cyclic investment networks. In such cases, bilateral contracting alone cannot prevent systemic risk; instead, an external entity must design a global collateral scheme covering all capital raisers. Moreover, the minimum total collateral needed to sustain efficient investment as a unique equilibrium can be arbitrarily higher in simple cyclic networks compared to their non-network counterparts. Finally, we establish computational complexity results applicable to both single enterprises and broader network structures.

This study examines the exact analytic solutions for gapped mode equations within the hydrodynamic approximation for a specific class of binary Bose-Einstein condensate acoustic black holes, where the horizon is generated by modulating phonon sound speed. By constructing asymptotic modes for various scattering processes, we derive exact scattering coefficients and decompose the field operator into these asymptotic states. The Unruh state is adopted as the suitable framework for describing the black hole's gravitational collapse, allowing for the calculation of outgoing mode particle densities. The effective energy gap term in the dispersion relation of gapped excitations establishes a threshold frequency, $\omega_r$, in the subsonic regime; below this frequency, propagating modes cannot exist. Consequently, the particle spectrum of the analogous Hawking modes outside the subsonic horizon significantly differs from gapless cases near $\omega_r$ due to a modified graybody factor that vanishes when the mode frequency drops below this threshold. Conversely, inside the supersonic horizon, the Hawking partner's particle production spectrum exhibits non-thermal characteristics. Furthermore, correlators between the analogue Hawking mode and its partner, which are relevant to experimental observations, are analyzed, revealing peaks near the threshold frequency $\omega_r$ caused by the gap energy term, features expected to be detectable in future experiments.

The Jump Inversion Theorem establishes that for any real $A$ with $A \ge_T 0'$, there exists a real $B$ such that $A \equiv_T B' \equiv_T B \oplus 0'$. It is known that $B$ can be selected from any special $\Pi^0_1$ subclass of $\{0,1\}^\omega$. This paper examines analogous refinements for two other significant theorems: the Join Theorem, which states that for all $A, Z$ satisfying $A \ge_T Z \oplus 0'$ and $Z >_T 0$, there is a $B$ such that $A \equiv_T B' \equiv_T B \oplus 0' \equiv_T B \oplus Z$; and the Pseudojump Inversion Theorem, which asserts that for all $A \ge_T 0'$ and every $e \in \omega$, there exists a $B$ such that $A \equiv_T B \oplus W_e^B \equiv_T B \oplus 0'$. We demonstrate that while $B$ can be found within certain special $\Pi^0_1$ subclasses of $\{0,1\}^\omega$ in these contexts, it cannot be found in others.

Photon-counting detector (PCD) X-ray technology provides superior spectral characterization, low noise, and high resolution, marking a new era for CT imaging and facilitating novel biomedical applications. However, involuntary patient motion causes artifacts in conventional CT, an issue that is exacerbated in PCD systems due to their extended scan times and large detector pitch. Moreover, the prevalence of defective pixels in PCDs complicates analytical image reconstruction, effectively eliminating current state-of-the-art motion correction techniques that rely on analytical methods. This paper extends our prior locally linear embedding (LLE) cone-beam motion correction approach to helical scanning geometries, a critical adaptation given the high expense of large-area PCDs. Beyond adapting LLE-based parametric searching for helical photon-counting CT, we introduce an unreliable-volume mask to enhance motion estimation precision and employ incremental updates on progressively refined sampling grids to optimize both efficiency and accuracy. Numerical simulations indicate that this method significantly reduces estimation errors at the longitudinal ends of the reconstructed volume and improves overall image quality. Clinical experiments on photon-counting scans of patient extremities confirm substantial resolution gains after applying our motion correction, uncovering fine structures that were previously obscured by motion blurring and artifacts.

Double source lensing offers a dimensionless ratio of distance ratios, effectively enabling a "remote view" of cosmology by comparing distances relative to a gravitational lens situated beyond the observer. This method allows us to test the cosmological framework, specifically regarding spatial curvature and the distance duality relation. We establish a consistency equation for constant spatial curvature, which facilitates the investigation of both flat versus curved geometries and the Friedmann-Lema\^itre-Robertson-Walker framework as a whole. Concerning distance duality, we show that the slope of the lens mass profile evolution must be constrained with a fractional precision at least five times tighter than any claimed violation of distance duality. Furthermore, utilizing LENSPOP forecasts for double source lensing systems within Euclid and LSST surveys, we examine constraints on dark energy equation of state parameters and potential evolution in the lens mass profile slope.

The predict-then-optimize framework aims to train a predictive model that maps environmental features to optimization parameters, thereby maximizing decision quality after the optimization is solved. Recent advances in decision-focused learning demonstrate that integrating the optimization problem directly into the training pipeline enhances decision quality and improves generalization to unseen tasks compared to using intermediate loss functions. This study applies this framework to sequential decision problems, specifically Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) solved via reinforcement learning. Given environment features and trajectory data from training MDPs, we train a predictive model capable of generalizing to unseen test MDPs lacking such trajectories. Two major computational hurdles exist when applying decision-focused learning to MDPs: (i) large state and action spaces render existing differentiation techniques infeasible, and (ii) the high-dimensional policy space, defined by neural networks, makes differentiating through the policy costly. We address the first challenge by sampling provably unbiased derivatives to approximate and differentiate through optimality conditions, and we tackle the second by employing a low-rank approximation of high-dimensional sample-based derivatives. We implement both Bellman-based and policy gradient-based decision-focused learning across three MDP problems with missing parameters, demonstrating that decision-focused learning yields superior generalization to unseen tasks.

We introduce a novel exponential framework for delay discounting that accounts for variations in impulsivity. This framework is shown to be dual to the two-parameter Tsallis delay discounting model introduced by Takahashi in 2007. We demonstrate that the model's parameters correspond to the mean and variance of impulsivity. These results offer an intuitive approach to understanding the emergence of the Tsallis distribution within social systems.
For every integer $g\ge 5$, we establish that any positive integer can be expressed as the sum of three palindromes in base $g$.

M33 X-7 stands as the sole identified eclipsing black hole high-mass X-ray binary, comprising a massive O supergiant donor and a heavy black hole within a compact orbit. Its exceptional X-ray brightness and position within the metal-poor galaxy M33 offer a singular opportunity to examine winds from metal-poor donor stars paired with black holes, shedding light on potential progenitors for black hole mergers. By employing phase-resolved simultaneous observations from HST and XMM-Newton, we tracked the interaction between the stellar wind and the black hole. A thorough spectroscopic analysis across X-ray, UV, and optical bands provided updated stellar and wind parameters that significantly diverge from earlier estimates. Specifically, component masses were substantially revised to 38 solar masses for the O-star donor and 11.4 solar masses for the black hole. The O giant overfills its Roche lobe and exhibits surface helium enrichment, while its densely clumped wind displays a mass-loss rate consistent with theoretical models. We examined contributions from various ions to wind driving and analyzed shifts in ionization structure caused by X-ray irradiation. Near the black hole, the wind is heavily suppressed due to intense X-ray illumination. Standard wind-fed accretion alone fails to account for the observed X-ray luminosity, suggesting an additional mass overflow that aligns with our acceleration calculations. X-ray photoionization generates an He II emission region producing $10^{47}$ photons per second. Using MESA, we calculated binary evolutionary tracks indicating the system is currently shifting toward an unstable mass transfer phase, forming a common envelope around the black hole and donor. Given the mass ratio of approximately 3.3 and the short orbital period, the system is unlikely to survive the common envelope phase and will instead merge.

Theoretical frameworks for black hole exteriors often mirror open quantum systems, where observable degrees of freedom interact with numerous unmeasurable ones beyond the event horizon. To establish a benchmark for more rigorous black hole calculations, a solvable Caldeira-Leggett model involving a quantum field coupled to unmeasured thermal modes on a common surface was introduced in arXiv:2106.09854. This work employs that model to evaluate two field-theoretic approximation schemes applicable to black hole dynamics: Open Effective Field Theory (EFT) techniques, which address the fields directly rather than Unruh-DeWitt detectors, and mean-field methods. Mean-field approaches are particularly relevant because the resulting effective Hamiltonians can exhibit nonlocality, a feature sometimes hypothesized for the near-horizon region of black holes. Meanwhile, Open EFTs track the evolution of the field state, enabling the analysis of thermalization and decoherence even at late times where perturbative methods break down. By applying both techniques to a solvable system, this study delineates their respective domains of validity and clarifies how their predictions compare to standard perturbative tools.

Although the backpropagation algorithm has driven the rapid advancement of deep learning, it depends heavily on vast amounts of labeled data and remains significantly distant from human learning mechanisms. The human brain efficiently acquires diverse concepts through self-organized, unsupervised processes enabled by the interplay of multiple learning rules and neural structures. While spike-timing-dependent plasticity (STDP) is a prevalent learning rule in the brain, spiking neural networks (SNNs) trained solely with STDP are inefficient and yield poor performance. Drawing inspiration from short-term synaptic plasticity, this paper proposes an adaptive synaptic filter and introduces an adaptive threshold balance as a neuron plasticity mechanism to enhance the representational capacity of SNNs. Additionally, an adaptive lateral inhibitory connection is incorporated to dynamically regulate spike balance, facilitating the learning of richer features. To accelerate and stabilize unsupervised SNN training, a sample temporal batch STDP method is designed to update weights based on multiple samples and time moments. Experiments conducted on MNIST and FashionMNIST demonstrate that the proposed model achieves state-of-the-art performance among current STDP-based unsupervised SNNs and exhibits significant advantages in few-shot learning scenarios.

Recently, generating stylized views from casually captured scenes has gained significant attention, with prior work typically representing scene geometry and appearance as neural point sets or neural radiance fields. Existing approaches often employ an image stylization method trained jointly or iteratively alongside the structure capture network; notably, the state-of-the-art SNeRF method alternates between training the NeRF and stylization networks. However, these methods suffer from high training times and necessitate joint optimization. In contrast, this paper introduces StyleTRF, a compact and rapid optimization strategy for stylized view generation based on TensoRF. By fine-tuning the appearance component using sparse stylized priors from a few rendered TensoRF views over several iterations, our approach effectively decouples style adaptation from view capture, achieving significantly faster performance than previous methods while delivering state-of-the-art results across multiple benchmark scenes.

Modular robots can be reconfigured daily into diverse designs to perform various tasks by creating a custom robot for each specific job. However, altering the mechanical structure alone is inadequate, as every configuration demands a distinct control policy. Crafting a policy from scratch for each new design is not scalable, particularly since even a limited set of modules can generate a vast array of configurations. Instead, we propose a modular policy framework where the policy architecture is conditioned on the hardware layout, enabling a single training process to manage a wide range of designs. Our method utilizes the fact that a modular robot's kinematics can be modeled as a design graph, with nodes representing modules and edges representing connections. For a given robot, we construct a corresponding policy graph with an identical structure, where each node houses a deep neural network, and modules of the same type share parameters (for instance, all legs on a hexapod utilize the same network weights). We employed a model-based reinforcement learning algorithm that combines model learning with trajectory optimization to train the policy. Our results demonstrate that the modular policy generalizes to numerous unseen designs without requiring additional learning. Finally, we show that the policy successfully controls various designs to achieve locomotion in both simulated and real-world environments.

The thermodynamic characteristics of a nonrelativistic free-electron Fermi gas hold fundamental significance in condensed matter physics. While internal energy, heat capacity, zero-field magnetic spin susceptibility, and pressure have been previously examined in three dimensions (3D) across low- and high-temperature limits, this study presents solutions for the temperature dependence of the chemical potential, internal energy, magnetic susceptibility, and constant-volume heat capacity spanning these regimes in 1D, 2D, and 3D. Additionally, we calculate pressure, enthalpy, constant-pressure heat capacity, isothermal compressibility, and the thermal expansion coefficient as functions of temperature for 2D and 3D systems. Of primary focus are the detailed dimension-dependent transitions between degenerate and nondegenerate temperature regimes for these properties, which are graphically illustrated for each case.

The phenomenological viability of inflation models involving axions and SU(2) gauge fields critically depends on managing the backreaction caused by particle production. While prior research largely relied on order-of-magnitude estimates to ensure that backreaction terms in the equations of motion for these fields remained negligible, this paper takes a more rigorous approach by solving the full equations of motion—including backreaction effects—across a broad spectrum of parameters for the spectator axion-SU(2) model. We first identify a novel slow-roll solution for the axion-SU(2) system when backreaction is absent. Subsequently, we derive precise conditions ensuring stable slow-roll dynamics in the presence of backreaction. Our analysis demonstrates that primordial gravitational waves generated by gauge fields can be amplified by a significant factor relative to standard quantum vacuum fluctuations without disrupting slow-roll evolution. By imposing constraints on scalar and tensor power spectra observed at CMB scales, we show the sourced contribution can exceed the vacuum contribution by over an order of magnitude. However, when additional constraints are applied regarding scalar modes non-linearly sourced by tensor modes, these two contributions remain comparable.

The logcosh loss function for neural networks was designed to merge the outlier-robustness of absolute error loss with the smooth, continuous derivatives of mean square error (MSE) near the mean, thereby facilitating the final stages of learning. It is evident and quickly observed that when processing clustered data, an artificial neural network (ANN) utilizing logcosh loss tends to model the dominant cluster rather than the average of both. Similarly, when applied to the regression of set-valued functions, a logcosh-based ANN converges toward a specific value from the available options—effectively learning one branch of the function—whereas an MSE-based ANN typically settles on a value between them. This study proposes a methodology employing ANNs with logcosh loss to identify the distinct branches of set-valued mappings within parameter-outcome sample sets and subsequently classify those samples based on their respective branches.

This paper introduces quantum monadic and quantum cylindric algebras, which represent adaptations of Halmos's monadic algebras and the cylindric algebras developed by Henkin, Monk, and Tarski to the quantum domain. Originally utilized in the algebraic analysis of classical and intuitionistic predicate logic, these structures find their primary examples within von Neumann algebras and subfactors in the quantum context. The work focuses on establishing the fundamental properties of these quantum algebras and exploring their connection to quantum predicate logic.

This study examines a network of cooperative agents tasked with local resource allocation under nonlinear model constraints. It prioritizes solutions that are anytime feasible, ensuring adherence to sum-preserving global constraints, a requirement common in various applications. The paper establishes sufficient conditions for such anytime (non-asymptotic) feasibility regarding the nonlinear mapping. Two distributed algorithms are proposed: one operates on directed, weight-balanced networks, while the other functions on undirected networks. The work details uniform quantization and introduces the concept of an $\epsilon$-accurate solution, providing an estimate of proximity to the exact optimizer across varying quantization levels. Furthermore, the approach addresses general strictly convex objective functions (potentially non-quadratic), demonstrating application in CPU allocation across a cloud of data centers using distributed methods. Ultimately, these results offer a coordination mechanism to optimally distribute tasks and CPU resources among networked servers, accounting for quantization limits and restricted server capacity.

Index Terms: multi-agent systems, sum-preserving resource allocation, distributed optimization, anytime feasibility

A principal finances a multi-stage project but reserves the right to terminate funding if progress stalls. The agent seeks to maximize the duration of this funding by strategically designing how project progress information is disclosed to the principal. If the project has strong initial prospects, the agent commits to revealing only positive updates confirming completion. Conversely, if the project's initial outlook is weak, the agent persuades the principal to begin funding by promising to disclose both favorable outcomes and unfavorable news regarding missed interim deadlines.
